identity.title: Rankl contributes to early bone development via the Wnt signaling pathway in zebrafish.

content.abstract: Receptor activator of nuclear factor-kappaB ligand (RANKL) is essential for osteoclast differentiation and bone remodeling; however, its role in early osteogenesis remains incompletely understood. This study investigated the contribution of RANKL to early bone development and regeneration and explored whether its effects on osteoblast differentiation are associated with RANK signaling, osteoclast activity, and the Wnt signaling pathway. Two zebrafish rankl mutant alleles were generated using CRISPR/Cas9, and the 19-bp insertion allele was used for phenotypic and mechanistic analyses. Bone mineralization and osteoclast formation were evaluated using Alizarin Red S and tartrate-resistant acid phosphatase staining, respectively. Osteoblast- and osteoclast-related gene expression was examined using quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction. Rescue experiments were performed using capped rankl mRNA, acute rank disruption, pharmacological osteoclast inhibition, and Wnt or mTOR pathway inhibitors. Transcriptomic profiling was used to identify signaling pathways associated with rankl deficiency. Compared with wild-type controls, rankl(-/-) zebrafish exhibited reduced skeletal mineralization at 8, 15, and 30 days post-fertilization and decreased expression of osteoblast-related genes. The number of TRAP-positive osteoclasts and the expression of osteoclast-related genes were also significantly reduced. Adult mutants exhibited increased vertebral thickness and narrowed neural and vascular canals, whereas caudal fin regeneration was delayed. Injection of capped rankl mRNA restored mineralization and osteoclast formation. Acute rank disruption blocked the osteoclast rescue but did not abolish the recovery of bone mineralization, while pharmacological osteoclast inhibition did not reproduce the early mineralization defect. Transcriptomic analysis identified enrichment of Wnt-related signaling, and several Wnt-associated genes were differentially expressed in rankl mutants. XAV939 attenuated the mineralization rescue induced by rankl mRNA, whereas rapamycin did not produce a comparable effect. These findings suggest that RANKL contributes to early zebrafish bone development through distinct effects on osteoclasts and osteoblasts. Osteoclast regulation is RANK-dependent, whereas the effect of RANKL on early osteogenesis may be partly independent of RANK-mediated osteoclastogenesis and associated with Wnt signaling. Further genetic and cell-specific studies are required to establish the underlying mechanism.
